key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems—not solar cells—reaching a roughly €3.53 million lifetime cost with fewer simulations than tested conventional optimizers.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation-intensive design effort for systems combining photovoltaics, storage, heating and other energy technologies.
method: Propose configuration changes using simulation history and structured memory.
Evaluate eight technology types through annual simulations and 25-year Net Present Cost.
Keep successful changes and automatically revert unsuccessful ones using git.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load case study, three LLM variants were tested in ten 50-simulation runs each; the best design cost 1.20% less than the best TPE result and 0.23% less than the best evolution-strategy result.
watch_item: Results come from a single case study, and reliability varied by LLM; broader validation and accounting for inference costs remain important.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
